extracted.intended_audience: LEA and SEA officials, district grant writers, education policy staff, and other education program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes federal ESSA rules and guidance on fund transferability, local flexibility demonstration agreement eligibility and requirements, LEA weighted per-pupil funding system requirements, consultation and expansion conditions, and program-level permitted uses and eligible entities (e.g., Alaska Native Education, Title I, arts, alternative certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: ESEA fund transferability restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: An SEA or LEA may not transfer funds it receives under any other ESEA program other than those listed here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates which programs funds can only be transferred to (never from) and which programs funds can be transferred to/from. This defines the permissible directions for intra-ESEA fund transfers by SEAs/LEAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs that may only receive transfers (never be source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can only be transferred to these programs, never from them: Title I, Part A: Improving Basic Programs Operated by LEAs; Title I, Part C: Education of Migratory Children; Title I, Part D: Neglected and Delinquent; Title III, Part A: English Language Acquisition; Title V, Part B: Rural Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs are enumerated as recipients that must not be treated as source programs for transfers; SEAs/LEAs cannot transfer funds out of these programs into others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs that may be sources and recipients of transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can be transferred to and from these programs: Title II, Part A: Supporting Effective Instruction; Title IV, Part A: Student Support and Academic Enrichment; Title IV, Part B: 21st Century Community Learning Centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs are explicitly listed as permitting bidirectional transfers (both to and from) among certain ESEA programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Local Flexibility Demonstration Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary is authorized to enter into local flexibility demonstration agreements with up to 50 LEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only LEAs may be parties to these demonstration agreements and the initial cap is 50 participating LEAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of Local Flexibility Demonstration Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreements are for not more than 3 years, but may be renewed for additional 3-year terms if the LEA has met requirements and is likely to continue to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewals depend on the LEA meeting the statutory/approved requirements and prospects for continued compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assurances required for LEA demonstration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide: a description of the school funding system based on weighted per-pupil allocations; a list of funding sources the LEA will include in the system; the amount and percentage of total LEA funding that will be allocated through the system; and per-pupil expenditures of State and local education funds and the per-pupil amount of eligible Federal funds for the preceding fiscal year for each school served by the LEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assurances are among 'other assurances' required in the application and establish baseline transparency about funding design and current/per-school per-pupil expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: allocation to school level based on per-pupil weighted formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The LEA’s school funding system must allocate a significant portion of funds, including State and local education funds and eligible Federal funds, to the school level based on the number of students in a school and a formula developed by the LEA that determines per-pupil weighted amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes school-level allocations driven by student counts and an LEA-developed weighting formula rather than allocations retained centrally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: greater weights for disadvantaged students
rubrics_metrics.description: The school funding system must allocate substantially more funding, using weights or allocation amounts, to English learners, students from low-income families, and students with any other characteristics associated with educational disadvantage chosen by the LEA, than to other students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs must demonstrably prioritize funding for identified disadvantaged groups through higher weights or allocations in the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: first-year funding floor for high-poverty schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that each high-poverty school receives, in the first year of the demonstration agreement, (1) more per-pupil funding for low-income students than in the year prior, and (2) at least as much per-pupil funding for English learners than in the year prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes minimum year-one funding improvement (for low-income students) and no reduction (for English learners) at high-poverty schools compared to the prior year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: significant percentage of LEA funds allocated through the system
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must be used to allocate to schools a significant percentage, as agreed upon during the application process, of all the LEA’s State and local education funds and eligible Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During application, LEA and Department agree what constitutes the 'significant percentage' to be routed through the weighted-per-pupil system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: include all school-level actual expenditures in calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: The LEA’s calculation of State and local education funds and eligible Federal funds that will be allocated must include all school-level actual expenditures, both personnel expenditures for instructional staff and non-personnel expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding baseline must encompass the full scope of school-level spending to ensure allocations reflect true resource levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued demonstration, annual safeguards and public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each LEA must demonstrate annually that, as compared to the previous year, no high-poverty school received less per-pupil funding for either low-income students or English learners. Each LEA must also make public detailed per-pupil expenditures for each school it serves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires year-to-year proof of non-reduction for protected groups at high-poverty schools and mandates public transparency of per-pupil expenditures by school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Flexibility for Equitable Per-Pupil Funding (ESEA Title I, Part E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to provide LEAs with flexibility to consolidate eligible Federal funds and State and local education funding in order to create a single school funding system based on weighted per-pupil allocations for low-income and otherwise disadvantaged students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the statutory aim: consolidation of funds to operate a unified, equity-focused weighted-per-pupil funding system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement for developing/implementing demonstration agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The LEA must develop and implement the local flexibility demonstration agreement in consultation with teachers, principals, other school leaders (including charter school leaders in a LEA that has charter schools), administrators of Federal programs impacted by the agreement, parents, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists required stakeholder groups to be included in the development and implementation process to ensure broad input and buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for expansion of demonstration agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the 2019–2020 academic year, the Secretary may extend funding flexibility to any LEA that submits and has approved an application, as long as a significant majority of the initial demonstration agreements with LEAs met, and continue to meet, the requirements as of the end of the 2018–2019 academic year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion from pilot to broader cohort depends on empirical success (majority meeting requirements) of initial demonstration agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alaska Native Education — eligible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible entities: Alaska Native organizations with experience operating programs that fulfill the purposes of this part of ESSA; Alaska Native organizations that do not have such experience but are in partnership with an SEA or an LEA or an Alaska Native organization that does have the requisite experience; an entity located in Alaska, and predominately governed by Alaska Natives, that does not meet the definition of an Alaska Native organization under this part of ESSA but has experience operating programs that fulfill the purposes of this part of ESSA, and is granted an official charter or sanction from at least one Alaska Native tribe or Alaska Native organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits experienced Alaska Native organizations, partnerships with SEA/LEA or experienced organizations, and certain locally governed Alaska entities with tribal sanction to be eligible applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alaska Native Education — permissible uses and program purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible uses include: education programs for at-risk urban Alaska Native students (improve proficiency/graduation; include data collection/evaluation); career and technical education support for regional vocational schools; certification and licensing programs for Alaska Native teachers/principals/school leaders; comprehensive school or community-based support services addressing family instability and trauma and improving conditions for learning; culturally-based education programs (Alaska Native history, culture, languages, immersion); curricula development that is culturally informed; enrichment programs (including STEM) with culturally appropriate supports; exchange and cross-cultural immersion programs; family and community engagement strategies; leadership academies; parental engagement; professional development for educators to address cultural diversity and needs; recruitment and preparation of Alaska Native teachers; remedial and enrichment programs; research and evaluation activities; school readiness including early childhood, home visiting, and native language immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a wide set of programmatic activities allowed under Title VI, Part C focused on culturally responsive education, supports, workforce development, and early childhood for Alaska Native populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative certification programs — permitted activities and eligible entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out programs that establish, expand, or improve alternative routes for State certification of teachers (especially for teachers of children with disabilities, English learners, STEM, or other shortage areas), principals, or other school leaders, for individuals with baccalaureate or master’s degrees, mid-career professionals, paraprofessionals, former military personnel, and recent graduates with records of academic distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible entity listed: SEAs; statutory reference: Supporting Effective Instruction State Grants (Title II, Part A). Emphasis on addressing shortage areas and widening routes into the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: American History and Civics Education — seminar/institute requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a Congressional Academy that offers a seminar or institute for outstanding students of American history and civics, which broadens and deepens understanding; led by a team of primary scholars and core teachers; conducted during the summer or other appropriate time; and of not less than 2 weeks and not more than 6 weeks in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies program leadership, target students, timing, and duration bounds for funded seminars/institutes under American History and Civics Education (Title II, Part B, Subpart 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts in Education — permissible activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting arts education for students (including disadvantaged students and students with disabilities) through activities such as professional development for arts educators/teachers/principals; development and dissemination of accessible instructional materials and arts-based educational programming (including online resources) in multiple arts disciplines; and community and national outreach activities that strengthen and expand partnerships among schools, LEAs, communities, or centers for the arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers professional learning, accessible materials/resources, and outreach/partnership-building as allowable arts education uses (Title IV, Part F, Subpart 4, section 4642).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part A — Grants to LEAs: permissible uses for at-risk students (schoolwide and targeted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible uses to address needs of all children, but particularly those at risk of not meeting State standards, including: implementation of a schoolwide tiered model to prevent/address problem behavior and early intervening services coordinated with IDEA; increasing amount and quality of learning time (expanded learning time, before/afterschool, summer); counseling, school-based mental health programs, specialized instructional support, mentoring, and other non-academic skills strategies; preparation for postsecondary education and the workforce including CTE and broadening access to postsecondary-credit coursework (AP/IB/dual enrollment/early college); professional development and data use; recruitment and retention of effective teachers (especially in high-need subjects); enriched and accelerated curriculum for well-rounded education; providing services to eligible children identified as having the greatest need for special assistance; schoolwide programs may establish/enhance preschool programs for children under 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists broad allowable activities under Grants to LEAs (Title I, Part A) for both schoolwide and targeted assistance models, emphasizing academic and non-academic supports, time expansion, workforce/postsecondary preparation, and staff development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted assistance programs — last-resort health/nutrition/social services clause
rubrics_metrics.description: If health, nutrition, and other social services are not otherwise available to eligible children in a targeted assistance school and such school has engaged in a comprehensive needs assessment and established a collaborative partnership with local service providers; and funds are not reasonably available from other public or private sources to provide such services, then a portion of the funds may be used as a last resort to provide such services (including basic medical equipment such as eyeglasses and hearing aids; compensation of a coordinator; family support and engagement services; integrated student supports; and professional development necessary to assist staff and parents in identifying and meeting comprehensive needs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows targeted assistance schools to use Title I funds as a last resort for critical health/nutrition/social supports but only under specified conditions (needs assessment, partnerships, exhaustion of other sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual/concurrent enrollment uses under schoolwide and targeted assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: A secondary school operating a schoolwide program may use funds to operate dual or concurrent enrollment programs that address needs of low-achieving secondary students and those at risk; a secondary school operating a targeted assistance program may use funds to provide dual or concurrent enrollment program services to eligible children identified as having the greatest need for special assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits use of Title I funds to support dual/concurrent enrollment both in schoolwide and targeted assistance contexts, including costs like tuition, fees, books, instructional materials, and transportation where appropriate.
